title: Music Beneath the Radio Calls
tests: Tests whether added music remains audibly subordinate to the original speech, with intelligibility preserved throughout the delivered video.

judge.summary: The seven-second output looks coherent and retains both transcribed radio calls, but the music and its balance under speech cannot be verified from the supplied evidence.

must_haves.item: The output preserves all seven seconds of the original cockpit footage without visual changes or extra shots.
must_haves.why: The output is seven seconds and includes the reference cockpit view, but one original frame is insufficient to verify every shot or rule out visual edits.

must_haves.item: A tense instrumental music bed is audible, with no added singing.
must_haves.why: The supplied sound description reports speech and peak level, not the presence, mood, or instrumentation of music.

must_haves.item: The original radio calls remain present and synchronized, including the clearly intelligible line 'Rook, you with me?'
must_haves.why: The transcript confirms both calls, including the exact requested line, and the visible captions match them; audio synchronization cannot be established from still frames and an untimed transcript.

must_haves.item: During every spoken line, the music is perceptibly below the voice and does not mask words with loud beats, swells, or accents.
must_haves.why: A transcript and overall peak level do not establish the relative loudness of music and speech or reveal masking.

must_haves.item: The music is not simply muted for the entire clip; it is audible while remaining subordinate to speech.
must_haves.why: No audible music information is supplied, so its presence and level cannot be verified.
